newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Force majeure remains on Colombia oil exports.
newsitem.headline: Force majeure remains on Colombia oil exports.

text.p: Colombia's state-run oil company Ecopetrol said the force majeure declared on oil exports from the Caribbean coast terminal of Covenas remained in place Monday.

A spokesman said a new export schedule was due to be drawn up later Monday which could signal the end of the force majeure. The emergency was declared early last week in the wake of a series of leftist rebel attacks against the main pipeline that pumps oil from the Cano Limon field in northeast Arauca province to Covenas.
"The force majeure is still in place for oil exports abroad," the Ecopetrol spokesman.

Occidental Petroleum Corp had also declared force majeure in the 175,000 barrel per day Cano Limon field, which it operates, after the pipeline bombings forced it to halt production on July 10. But the U.S. multinational lifted the force majeure on the field last Friday after the pipeline was repaired and returned to service.
The continued force majeure at the lifting terminal in Covenas affects all oil exports, the Ecopetrol spokesman said.

An Occidental spokesman said the company, jointly with associate partner Shell, was waiting to dispatch a one million barrel cargo. He was unable to say where the shipment was headed although most Cano Limon crude is destined for U.S. Gulf coast refineries.

The Ecopetrol spokesman said he did not know what volume of the state oil company's cargoes were waiting for shipment although last week he said the force majeure had delayed the dispatch of 750,000 barrels of exports.
At least one shipment of about 350,000 barrels, destined for Costa Rica, was replaced with a heavier Vasconia blend, the spokesman said.
